body: THE GOOD NUMBER: screener-perfect: ROCE 37-43%, OPM ~25%, borrowings cut from Rs 416 cr (FY15) to zero (FY18), PAT Rs 322 -> 680 cr in three years, and CFO was positive and above PAT in FY17-18 (Rs 669 cr, Rs 530 cr), so even our CFO/PAT test passed. The stock ran to ~Rs 515 (Jan 2018). WHY IT LIED: a network of franchised rural kiosks for banking, e-governance and e-commerce is a thin-margin, low-ticket business; 25% operating margins and 40% ROCE were out of line with every comparable. In FY18 sales jumped 63% to Rs 6,502 cr while OPM fell from 24% to 15%, signalling a mix shift into low-value trading. Debtor days were 157 in FY15. PwC resigned in Apr 2018; the stock fell ~84%; FY19 revenue collapsed to Rs 1,508 cr and debtor days went to 319, 729 and 1,301 (FY19-21). It trades at ~Rs 5 (Nov 2026). TEST: rebuild unit economics bottom-up (revenue per outlet x outlets x margin) and compare with the reported total; treat a sudden revenue-mix shift plus a parabolic price as a request for evidence. LESSON: CFO/PAT can pass in a trap; numbers that are too good for the business's physics are a flag on their own.

data.good_number: ROCE 37-43% (FY15-18), OPM 24-26%, debt cut to zero by FY18, PAT Rs 680 cr, CFO Rs 669 cr (FY17) > PAT
data.test_that_catches_it: margin vs business physics and peers; revenue mix shifts; parabolic price; auditor resignation
data.why_misleading: economics far above what a rural kiosk/e-governance franchise business can earn; sales jumped and margin halved in FY18 as low-margin trading was added; then revenue collapsed 77%

title: Hidden trap: Vakrangee's 40% ROCE, zero debt and positive CFO
